'''Octave Levenspiel''' (January 1, 1926 – March 5, 2017)  was a professor of [[chemical engineering]] at [[Oregon State University]] (OSU). His principal interest was [[chemical reaction engineering]], and he was the author of a major textbook ''Chemical Reaction Engineering'' as well as numerous research publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=Octave Levenspiel|url=http://www.gazettetimes.com/albany/news/local/obituaries/octave-levenspiel/article_ed1f250a-bace-5ee3-be0c-165344905a58.html|publisher=Corvalis Gazette Times|accessdate=11 April 2017}}</ref>

==Life==
Levenspiel was born in [[Shanghai]], [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]], in 1926, the son of Abe and Lily Levenspiel, who were [[Polish people|Polish]] [[Jews]] who had gone to China to escape oppression in Europe.<ref name=Turner>Robin Turner ''The Chemical Engineer'' April 2017 p 57 "Obituary: Octave Levenspiel (1926&ndash;2017)"</ref> At the age of 15, he was on a ship to the US when the [[Attack on Pearl Harbor]] occurred, so he was interned in [[Manila]] until the [[Victory over Japan Day|end of the war]].<ref name=Turner/>  In the US, he graduated with a bachelor's degree from [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]] in 1947.  He obtained his PhD from OSU in 1952, and after a period teaching at other schools returned to OSU where he spent the remainder of his career, retiring in 1991 but continuing as emeritus professor.<ref name=Turner/>

In 1952 he married Mary Jo Smiley and they had three children.  He died on March 5, 2017.<ref name=Turner/>

==Work==
The [[Levenspiel plot]] is named after him.

Levenspiel was well known among his students for his ability to do quick [[back-of-the-envelope calculations]]. [[GNU Octave]], a high-level language primarily intended for numerical computations and developed by John W. Eaton, a former student of Octave Levenspiel, is named after him.

==Books==
All of Levenspiel's books listed below have been translated to several other languages.

*''Chemical Reaction Engineering'', Wiley; 3 Sub edition (August 13, 1998), {{ISBN|0-471-25424-X}}
*''The Chemical Reactor Omnibook'', Oregon St Univ Bookstores (January 1993),  {{ISBN|0-88246-160-5}}
*''Fluidization Engineering'' (coauthored), Butterworth-Heinemann Ltd; (October 1991), {{ISBN|0-409-90233-0}}
*''Engineering Flow and Heat Exchange'', Plenum Pub Corp (Dez. 1984), {{ISBN|0-306-41599-2}}
*''Understanding Engineering Thermo'', Prentice Hall PTR; (September 4, 1996), {{ISBN|0-13-531203-5}}
*''Rambling through Science and Technology'', Lulu, 2007

==Awards==
*R.H. Wilhelm award ([[American Institute of Chemical Engineers|AIChE]])
*W.K. Lewis award ([[American Institute of Chemical Engineers|AIChE]])
*Founders award with gold medal ([[American Institute of Chemical Engineers|AIChE]])
*ChE Lectureship award ([[American Society for Engineering Education|ASEE]])
*P.V. Danckwerts award ([[Institution of Chemical Engineers|IChemE]])
*Honorary doctorates from France, Serbia, and the Colorado School of Mines
*Elected into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] (2000)
*Amundson award (ISCRE/NASCRE) (2001)
